name: Jon's Product Feed for Google Merchant Center
author: Jon Webb

sections.description:
JRA Google Merchant Feed connects your WooCommerce store to Google Merchant Center using the Content API for Shopping – it does not rely on generating and uploading feeds so all changes are reflected instantly on Google. It supports full and delta sync, attribute and term mappings, per-product and per-category exclusions, Google product category mapping, custom labels, and availability date from lead time and due date meta. Tested on multiple live sites with real world issues solved.

Some of the great features include:
* Attribute mapping that actually works!
* Offer ID mapping to preserve ids of products already on google from previous feeds
* Live sync pushes products to Google Merchant centre with no delay
* Live check button on each product to see status of product on Google Merchant centre
* Generate report from Google of all issues, with links to products with issues
* Set default Google product category, and map Google product category to each of your product categories
* Map individual Terms of your attributes to Google required values such as Gender: “Mens” -> male, “Womens” -> female
* Set availability dates and lead times so out-of-stock products can be listed on Google Merchant centre
* Manual and Cron (regular) sync pushes to Google
* And much more

External Services

This plugin connects to Google’s APIs to provide its core functionality.

Google Merchant Center Content API for Shopping

When you sync products, data including product title, description, price, availability, images, SKU, brand, GTIN/MPN, Google product category, and mapped attributes is sent to Google Merchant Center via the Google Content API for Shopping. Data is transmitted when you trigger a sync manually or via the scheduled automatic sync. No data is sent until you configure and connect the plugin.

Service provided by Google LLC.
* Google Terms of Service
* Google Privacy Policy
* Content API for Shopping documentation

Google Product Taxonomy

When you click “Refresh taxonomy” in the plugin settings, a request is made to fetch Google’s public product taxonomy file from google.com. The taxonomy is stored locally in your WordPress database and used to power the category search. No personal data is sent in this request.

Service provided by Google LLC.
* Google Terms of Service
* Google Privacy Policy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to Merchant Feed > Settings to configure your Google API credentials.
